newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony develops high-capacity optical disc.
newsitem.headline: Sony develops high-capacity optical disc.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Tuesday that it has developed technology for high-capacity recordable optical discs that can hold nearly five times more information than that of recordable DVD-RAMs.
Sony plans to start selling the product by 2000, a Sony spokesman said.
Sony's new disc will be able to store 12 gigabytes of information on a single side of a disc that is the size of a CD, or about five hours of TV programmes, Sony said.
In case of high-precision pictures, such as those of high-definition TVs, it will be able to record 1.2 hours of motion pictures, Sony said.
"We see it as a medium for recording video, while we plan to sell smaller capacity DVD-RAMs as computer-use recording media," the spokesman said.
DVD-RAMs, which will hit the market by the end of this year, can hold 2.6 gigabytes of information at present, about one-hour of ordinary-format motion pictures.
Sony said the high capacity has been achieved through the use of a newly developed high-power blue-green laser, a two element objective lens and a 1.2 mm-thick disc.
